assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reshaped how economists and policymakers understand technology, trade exposure, task content of jobs and local labour-market adjustment. Combines credible empirical design with conceptual frameworks and has changed both academic work and public debate. The adjustment costs of technological and trade change are an important, general theme.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to both the task framework and the trade-shock work. Hanson is central to the local labour-market effects of import competition. Katz is credited mainly through the long-running skill-premium and education-versus-technology literature. Dorn is a key co-author of the China-shock papers and a plausible alternative to Katz. The task approach also draws on Levy, Murnane and others, and Acemoglu has already been recognised for related work.
assessment.maturity: The China-shock and task papers are 10 to 20 years old and have been widely replicated and extended. The skill-premium work is older still. Timing looks mature.
uncertainties: Which of Katz or Dorn should be paired with Autor and Hanson.
Overlap with the 2023 prize (Goldin) and the 2024 prize (Acemoglu) on technology, skills and inequality.
Debate over the magnitude and persistence of the China shock and over measurement of task changes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection into exporting transformed trade theory and empirics. The framework explains gains from trade through reallocation across firms and supports a large body of quantitative work. It is a foundational advance beyond the new trade theory recognised in 2008.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the core contribution. Helpman, with Melitz and Yeaple, extended it to exporting versus foreign direct investment, and Helpman has broader foundational trade work. Redding's contributions are important but more in quantitative extensions and spatial models. Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have strong claims to the empirical origins and are outside this candidate's credited names.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of confirmation, extension and use in policy analysis. Mature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees it as incremental to the 2008 prize.
Credit allocation among Melitz, Helpman, Redding and uncredited empirical pioneers.
Helpman also appears in a separate trade candidate, so there is overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Built the modern theory and empirics of political economics, covering electoral rules, constitutions, fiscal policy and state capacity. This bridges economics and political science and has produced testable predictions that have been taken up empirically. It is a coherent, original research programme.
assessment.attribution: Persson and Tabellini are the clearest joint authors of the unified framework and the constitutional-economics evidence. Besley's contributions to state capacity, accountability and development politics are equally strong. The trio is a natural grouping. Other political-economy theorists such as Alesina and Acemoglu overlap, and Acemoglu was recognised in 2024.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of development, with a large body of confirmatory empirical work. Mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2024 prize on institutions and political economy.
Some reduced-form results on electoral rules are sensitive to specification and identification.
Alesina's death may affect how the field's credit is divided.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework underpins how central banks analyse and conduct monetary policy, including inflation targeting and the Taylor rule. Practical influence is very large, and the micro-founded nominal-rigidity model gave policy analysis a common language.
assessment.attribution: Credit is widely spread across Calvo (pricing), Taylor (rules and staggered contracts), Woodford (the canonical synthesis), Gali (and Gertler, on the Phillips curve and policy), Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans (medium-scale DSGE) and Smets-Wouters. Any three-person selection is partial and contestable. Gertler's links to the 2022 prize and to the financial accelerator add complexity.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of development, with extensive use and confirmation in practice. Though some parts were challenged after 2008 and 2021-22 inflation, the framework has been adapted rather than discarded.
uncertainties: Severe attribution problem with eight credited names and a diffuse intellectual history.
Performance of the framework during the post-2020 inflation.
Overlap with earlier macro prizes.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Showed quantitatively that misallocation of inputs across firms can account for a large share of cross-country income gaps. This linked micro-level data to aggregate development and productivity, and it has reshaped growth and development accounting. It is a general contribution with major policy relevance.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow (2009) is the central paper and the pair is the natural core. Restuccia and Rogerson (2008) is a parallel contribution, and Restuccia is credited here but Rogerson is not. The earlier growth-accounting tradition is also relevant.
assessment.maturity: About 17 years of heavy use, with many replications and extensions in many countries. Reasonably mature.
uncertainties: Measurement concerns: measurement error and unobserved heterogeneity may inflate measured misallocation.
Whether the committee prefers to wait given the two Restuccia-Rogerson and Hsieh-Klenow strands.
Overlap with the 2025 growth prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The demand-estimation and dynamic-industry methods now form the backbone of empirical industrial organisation. They are used in merger review, competition policy and pricing analysis. The contribution is mainly methodological but with very wide practical use.
assessment.attribution: BLP (Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes) is the clear core, and Pakes's separate work on dynamic games and on estimation with Ericson, Olley and others adds to his claim. Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin have separate claims on market structure and dynamic estimation, so the credited group is broader than three.
assessment.maturity: Developed 1990s to 2000s and widely confirmed in application. Mature.
uncertainties: Methodological prizes are less certain to rank above substantive discoveries.
Credit boundaries with Bresnahan, Reiss and others.
Sensitivity of results to functional form and instruments.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The intertemporal open-economy framework (the 'Redux' model) and the exchange-rate disconnect work provide the microfounded foundation of modern international macroeconomics. Their textbook and policy influence is substantial, and the disconnect puzzles remain central empirical questions.
assessment.attribution: Obstfeld and Rogoff are the natural pair for the 1995 model and the disconnect and puzzles literature. Other contributors, such as Gali, Monacelli, Lane and Gourinchas, and Rey, extended the open-economy framework. Rogoff also has a separate nomination in B007, which may split support.
assessment.maturity: Three decades of use. The framework is mature and widely adopted, though it was refined as much as confirmed.
uncertainties: Some of the work is a theoretical framework whose empirical validation is partial; the puzzles are still unresolved.
Overlap with the New Keynesian candidate.
Split of Rogoff's support across two candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Placed legal institutions, investor protection and ownership at the centre of comparative financial development and corporate governance. It launched a very large cross-country literature and shifted how economists think about institutions and finance.
assessment.attribution: The LLSV group (La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer, Vishny) is a tight, clearly attributable collaboration. Only three can be proposed and Vishny is left out here. Shleifer also has wider contributions in behavioural finance and corporate finance, which could strengthen or complicate a case. The institutions literature is also linked to the 2024 laureates.
assessment.maturity: More than 25 years of use, with a substantial body of critique and revision. Mature in age, but contested in empirical content.
uncertainties: Substantial criticism of the legal-origins identification and of the construction of the indices.
Overlap with the 2024 institutions prize.
Which three of four co-authors would be named, and whether non-scientific considerations around individuals matter.
